questions.question: A shop owner generates the same prompt three times and gets three different images. What is the most likely reason?
options: The tool searched the internet and found three different photos.
Each generation started from different random noise, so details not in the prompt were filled in differently.
The prompt was written incorrectly, so the tool could not understand it.
The tool is broken and should always return the same image.
questions.explanation: Generators build each image from random starting noise, set by a seed, so unlisted details change between runs. The most tempting wrong option is that the prompt was written incorrectly. Variation is normal even with a good prompt; the fix is to describe the details you want to keep, not to assume an error.

questions.question: Which term describes the shape of an image, such as 1:1 for a square or 9:16 for a phone story?
options: Seed
Model
Reference image
Aspect ratio
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio is the width-to-height shape of the image. The most tempting wrong option is seed, because it is also a setting with numbers. A seed sets the starting noise and changes what appears, not the shape of the frame.

questions.question: Which change to the prompt 'a beautiful cup' will most improve the image for a café menu?
options: Add 'stunning, amazing, ultra detailed, high quality'.
Repeat the word 'beautiful' three times for emphasis.
Replace it with 'a white ceramic cup with a thin gold rim on a marble counter, soft morning light from the right'.
Make the prompt shorter: 'cup'.
questions.explanation: Specific, visible details such as material, setting and light direction give the model something it can draw. The most tempting wrong option is adding praise words like 'stunning' and 'high quality'. They sound helpful but describe nothing visible, so the model still has to guess.

questions.question: A learner wants a wide 16:9 image. Which approach matches how the two tools are usually controlled?
options: In Adobe Firefly choose the aspect ratio in the settings panel; in Gemini ask for the format in the prompt or conversation.
In both tools the aspect ratio can only be changed after download.
In Gemini choose the aspect ratio from a settings panel; in Firefly type it in a chat.
Neither tool can produce a wide image, so it must be cropped in Canva.
questions.explanation: Firefly is controlled mainly through menus and settings, while Gemini is controlled mainly through conversation. The most tempting wrong option reverses the two tools. Remember that interfaces change often, so always check the live tool.

questions.question: A travel agent keeps the same garden scene but changes only 'soft overcast light' to 'golden hour sunlight'. What should change most in the new image?
options: The camera angle and framing of the scene.
The objects in the garden, such as the trees and the gate.
The aspect ratio of the image.
The warmth of the light and the length of the shadows.
questions.explanation: Golden hour means warm, low sunlight, so the light colour and shadows change the mood. The most tempting wrong option is the camera angle. The composition words were not changed, so the framing should stay about the same; this is why changing one part at a time is useful.
